subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should Codex app-server WebSocket and Unix upgrade handshakes enforce an unconditional 30-second limit, or should that limit derive from the existing app-server request budget?
rationale: The patch fixes a real indefinite wait, but the repository supports custom remote WebSocket endpoints and a hard timeout changes their runtime compatibility contract; direct sibling Codex source inspection was unavailable in this sandbox, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary.

options.title: Keep the 30-second floor
options.body: Remove the unrelated CodeQL edit and explicitly approve 30 seconds as the Codex transport handshake contract for both TCP and Unix paths.

options.title: Derive from request timeout
options.body: Use the existing app-server request timeout as the handshake budget so one owner-controlled value governs connection and initialization waits.

options.title: Pause for upstream contract proof
options.body: Hold the PR until upstream Codex lifecycle behavior and a real Unix-socket stalled-handshake run confirm the desired terminal events and timeout.

recommendation.title: Keep the 30-second floor
recommendation.body: Remove the unrelated CodeQL edit and explicitly approve 30 seconds as the Codex transport handshake contract for both TCP and Unix paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They appear most closely connected to the introduction and subsequent remote-transport evolution of the Codex app-server integration.
